BANDALA MLCJOO Office of the MLGOO Municipality of Bilar, Bohol Dear Ms. Bandala: This is in reference to the 2nd Indorsement dated 06 July 2018 from DILG Regional Office VII of your letter dated II June 2018 and letter dated 30 May 2018 of Ms. Silvina C. Lumantas of Brgy. Yanaya, Bilar, Bohol. As represented by Ms. Lumantas in her letter, Mr. Bob Joseph D. Corpus is one of the newly elected Sangguniang Barangay Members and Mr. Joseph D. Corpus won as Sangguniang Kabataan Chairperson. They are both from Yanaya, Bilar, Bohol. Thus, Ms. Lumantas is filing a complaint before your office on the alleged violation of the anti-political dynasty provision as she believed that political dynasty is not allowed. Foremost, the qualification on anti-political dynasty is provided under RA 10742 otherwise known as the Sangguniang Kabataan Reform Act of 2015. However, DILG has no jurisdiction to determine whether a candidate violated the qualifications under Section IO of said law which provides: SECTION IO. Qualifications. —An official of the Sangguniang Kabataan, either elective or appointee, must be a citizen of the Philippines, a qualified voter of the Katipunan ng Kabataan, a resident of the barangay for not less than one (I) year immediately preceding the day of the elections, at least eighteen (18) years but not more than twenty-four (24) years of age on the day of the elections, able to read and write Filipino, English, or the local dialect, musc not be related within the second civil degree ofconsapguinity QU affinity to any incumbent elected national official or to apy incumbent elected regional: provincial. city, munici Hicial h r she seeks Page 1 of3

must not have been convicted by final judgment of any crime in volving moral turpitude. (emphasis ours) Under the law, it is the trial courts of limited jurisdiction (e.g. Municipal Trial Court) which has jurisdiction on the issue relative to the elective officials in the Barangay levell. Moreover, Section 2 (2), Article IX (C), of the 1987 Philippine Constitution, provides that: "Sec. 2. The Commission on Elections shall exercise the following powers and functions: all contests relating to the elections, returns, and qualifications of all elective regional, provincial, and city officials, and appellate jurisdiction over all contests involving elective municipal officials decided by trial courts of general jurisdiction. or involving elective Ifi flimi Therefore, it is the Municipal Trial Court which has jurisdiction on the question relative to the qualification of an elective official in the Barangay. Meanwhile, even if this Department has no power to decide on the qualification of the elective officials, it would like to give its view of the herein issue on the alleged violation of anti-political dynasty. As cited above, Section 10 of RA 10742 provides that an elective or appointive official in the SK "must not be related within the second civil degree of consanguinity or affinity national official or to any incumbent elected regional, provincial, city, municipal, or barangay official, in the locality where he or she seeks to be elected". In the herein case, Ms. Lumantas said that Mr. Bob Joseph D. Corpus is a NEWLY elected Sangguniang Barangay Member and his brother Joseph D. Corpus won as Sangguniang Kabataan Chairperson. It must be noted that at the time of the filing of candidacy and during the conduct of elections, there is no incumbent elected official related to Mr. Joseph D. Corpus within 2nd civil degree of consanguinity or affinity as his brother is not considered elected yet but merely a candidate. Thus, this Department has the opinion that there is no violation of Anti-political dynasty provision under RA 10742. However, this Department's opinion is without prejudice to the view that will be taken by the COMELEC or the courts on this matter, and we shall defer to the said opinion and/or decision.
